content.label: What happened
content.takeaway: A config typo took checkout down for 47 minutes; detection, status updates and review all lagged.

nodes.title: A config typo cut the payments connection pool from 50 to 5

content.markdown:
On Friday, March 14 at 16:40, a config change set the gateway connection pool from 50 connections to 5 (the intent was 55). Checkout requests queued for a connection and timed out.

- Alert fired at 17:02, 22 minutes after the change
- Config rolled back at 17:15; checkout recovered at 17:27
- 47 minutes of errors: about 2,300 failed checkouts, 140 support tickets before the status page went up

nodes.title: The alert worked as configured, but too slowly for checkout

content.markdown: It only fires when the checkout error rate stays above 10% for 15 minutes. Errors crossed 10% around 16:47, so 17:02 was the earliest it could fire. Leila: 15 minutes of sustained errors is too long when every minute is lost revenue.

nodes.title: The status page went up 40 minutes late

content.markdown: Posted at 17:20, 40 minutes after errors began, while customers were already asking on social media. The incident commander posts it when they remember; on Friday that was Marcus, who was busy rolling back.
Config is edited in the deploy dashboard and applied directly: code changes need two approvals, config needs none. Tomás: a typo in code would have been caught by a reviewer or a test.

content.label: Agreed decisions
content.takeaway: Three changes were agreed in the meeting.

content.markdown: **Agreed.** Lower the checkout error-rate alert from 10% over 15 minutes to 5% over 5 minutes. Over the last 30 days it would have paged twice on noise, both during the payment provider's maintenance; the group accepted that.
**Agreed.** Support can post a status-page update directly, without waiting for the incident commander.

nodes.title: Payments config goes through pull-request review

content.markdown: **Agreed.** Payments config moves into the repo; every change gets a pull request and one approval from the payments team.

content.label: Proposed, not agreed
content.takeaway: Two proposals discussed without agreement; both stay open.

nodes.title: A Friday deploy freeze was proposed and disputed

content.markdown:
Tomás proposed stopping all payments deploys after 15:00 on Fridays: this change went out at 16:40 on a Friday with half the team logged off.

**Disagreement**
- Leila: a freeze moves the risk to Monday morning, when traffic is higher; the cause was the missing review, not the day.
- Tomás: fewer people around slows recovery for any cause.
- Leila: recovery took 25 minutes after the alert, with Marcus on call.

**Status:** not agreed and not decided; Tomás will bring incident data to the next review.

nodes.title: Automatic rollback was proposed; migrations make it uncertain

content.markdown:
Marcus proposed rolling back automatically when the checkout error rate doubles within 10 minutes of a deploy.

- Leila: maybe for config; for code, rolling back without its database migration can leave things worse.
- Marcus: releases with migrations could be excluded.
- Leila wants to know how often migrations ship before agreeing.

**Status:** left open; nobody knows how many releases include migrations.

content.label: Action items
content.takeaway: Owners and dates as stated in the meeting; the email has no date.

items.text: Marcus: change the checkout alert to 5% over 5 minutes, by Wednesday, March 19
Leila: move payments config into the repo and add the approval rule, by Friday, March 21
Tomás: pull six months of incidents and check whether late-Friday deploys are over-represented; bring it to the next review on April 2
Kenji: draft the customer email (no deadline set)

nodes.title: Did customers retry the 2,300 failed checkouts?

content.markdown: Nobody knows yet: the payment logs would show it, but no one has looked. The answer changes what the email to customers says.
